=== FILE: references/design/daisyui-patterns.md === # DaisyUI Patterns
DaisyUI component patterns for AIUX apps. All classes use the `aiux-` prefix (DaisyUI v5).
**Source of truth:** The project's `@servicenow/aiux` dependency (declared in `package.json`). This metapackage transitively provides the `tailwind.css` with `@source inline()` safelists. Only classes registered there are available at runtime. Always verify against the installed metapackage — do NOT assume availability.
---
## Prefix Convention
All DaisyUI classes in AIUX use the `aiux-` prefix:
```html <!-- Standard DaisyUI → AIUX prefixed --> <button class="aiux-btn aiux-btn-primary">Click</button> <div class="aiux-card aiux-card-border">...</div> <span class="aiux-badge aiux-badge-success">Active</span> ```
### Safelist Registration
DaisyUI classes must be registered via `@source inline()` in the project's `tailwind.css` to prevent tree-shaking. This file is provided transitively through `@servicenow/aiux` in `package.json`. After `pnpm install`, check the resolved `tailwind.css` in `node_modules` to see which classes are safelisted for the installed version.
---

## Verifying Availability
The safelist lives in the installed metapackage at `node_modules/@servicenow/aiux/components/core/src/styles/tailwind.css`. Always verify before using a class:
```bash # Confirm the file exists ls node_modules/@servicenow/aiux/components/core/src/styles/tailwind.css
# Search for a specific class grep "aiux-skeleton" node_modules/@servicenow/aiux/components/core/src/styles/tailwind.css ```
If a class is not safelisted, it will be tree-shaken and silently fail at runtime. Options:
1. Use an alternative that IS safelisted 2. Implement the styles manually in the component's `static styles` 3. Request the platform team add it to the metapackage
---
## Accessibility Requirements Per Component
### Buttons
- Visible focus ring (`:focus-visible`) - `aria-label` when icon-only - `aria-disabled="true"` + `pointer-events: none` instead of `disabled` attribute when needed
### Modals
```html <dialog class="aiux-modal" aria-modal="true" role="dialog" aria-labelledby="modal-title" > <div class="aiux-modal-box"> <h3 id="modal-title">${i18n.getMessage('Confirm Action')}</h3> <div class="aiux-modal-action"> <button class="aiux-btn" @click="${this._close}"> ${i18n.getMessage('Cancel')} </button> <button class="aiux-btn aiux-btn-primary" @click="${this._confirm}"> ${i18n.getMessage('Confirm')} </button> </div> </div> </dialog> ```
### Toggles
- Always pair with a visible `<label>` - Use `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`
### Tabs
- `role="tablist"` on container - `role="tab"` + `aria-selected` on each tab - `role="tabpanel"` on content
---
## Key Rules
1. **Semantic colors directly** — `bg-primary`, `bg-success`, etc. 2. **DaisyUI components carry their own rounding** — add only classes that change the component's variant or size 3. **Card surfaces** — `bg-base-100 shadow-sm` 4. **Collapse** — native `<details>/<summary>` elements 5. **Tooltips** — tooltip directive from `@servicenow/aiux-directive-tooltip` 6. **Disabled state** — native `disabled` attribute on the element 7. **Skeleton loaders** — `aiux-skeleton` class; for animated variants use `static styles` CSS (see `css-custom-properties.md`) 8. **Modals** — `<dialog>` element 9. **Non-blocking alerts** — `aiux-alert aiux-alert-{info|success|warning|error} aiux-alert-soft` 10. **Status chips** — `aiux-badge aiux-badge-sm aiux-badge-{success|warning|error} aiux-badge-soft` 11. **Async loading in buttons** — add `aiux-loading aiux-loading-spinner aiux-loading-xs` inside the button while `_saving` is true
---
## Card Pattern
```html <!-- Elevated card --> <div class="aiux-card bg-base-100 shadow-sm"> <div class="aiux-card-body p-6"> <h2 class="aiux-card-title text-base font-medium text-text-primary"> ${i18n.getMessage('Card Title')} </h2> <p class="text-sm text-text-tertiary">${this._description}</p> <div class="aiux-card-actions justify-end mt-2"> <button class="aiux-btn aiux-btn-primary aiux-btn-sm"> ${i18n.getMessage('Action')} </button> </div> </div> </div>
<!-- Bordered card --> <div class="aiux-card aiux-card-border bg-base-100"> <div class="aiux-card-body">...</div> </div>
<!-- Card wrapping slotted content --> <div class="aiux-card bg-base-100 shadow-sm"> <slot></slot> </div> ```
---
## Badge Pattern
```html <span class=${classMap({ 'aiux-badge': true, 'aiux-badge-success': this._status === 'active', 'aiux-badge-warning': this._status === 'pending', 'aiux-badge-error': this._status === 'error' })}> ${this._statusLabel} </span> ```
---
## Dropdown Menu Pattern
```html <div class="aiux-dropdown aiux-dropdown-end"> <button tabindex="0" class="aiux-btn aiux-btn-ghost aiux-btn-sm"> <aiux-icon name="ellipsis-vertical-outline" size="sm"></aiux-icon> </button> <ul tabindex="0" class="aiux-dropdown-content aiux-menu p-2 shadow bg-base-100 rounded-box w-52" > <li><a @click="${this._handleEdit}">${i18n.getMessage('Edit')}</a></li> <li><a @click="${this._handleDelete}">${i18n.getMessage('Delete')}</a></li> </ul> </div> ```

=== FILE: references/quality/validation-rules.md === # Validation Rules
Automated assertions to validate AIUX components. Run after every implementation.
---
## Component Structure
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Base class | Class extends `AIUXElement` or `AIUXWidgetElement` | Error | | Custom element tag | `@customElement('tag-name')` with unique namespaced tag | Error | | Export | Widget has `export default` | Error | | Constructor | `super()` called first | Error | | connectedCallback | `super.connectedCallback()` called | Error | | disconnectedCallback | `super.disconnectedCallback()` called | Error | | Static properties type | Every entry has `type` key | Error | | State declaration | Every `this._*` assignment has matching `state: true` | Error | | Property init | All properties have defaults in constructor | Warning |
---
## Widget-Specific
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | | Discoverable | `@discoverable(true)` present | Error | | bestFor | `@bestFor('...')` with meaningful description | Error | | Name | `@name('...')` decorator | Warning | | Description | `@description('...')` decorator | Warning | | Server decorator | If server.js exists → `@server('./server.js')` present | Error | | Render states | `render()` handles loading, error, empty, data | Warning | | Widget height | `:host` has `height: 100%` | Warning |
---
## Server Script
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Export | `export default function server(data, _options, input)` | Error | | Security | Using `GlideRecordSecure` (not `GlideRecord`) | Error | | Field selection | GlideQuery `.select()` used when restricting fetched columns (GlideRecord has no field-selection API) | Warning | | Limit | `setLimit()` called before `query()` | Error | | Access check | `canRead()` after `get()` | Warning | | Error shape | `data.isError` + `data.errorMessage` includes actual error (`e.message`), not generic string alone | Error | | Input validation | `input.*` has defaults | Warning | | Server strings | `gs.getMessage()` for user-facing text | Warning | | Truncation data | If `setLimit()` is used, server returns `data.hasMore` and `data.totalAvailable` via `GlideAggregate` | Warning | | Truncation UI | Client renders a truncation notice (e.g. "Showing X of Y") when `hasMore` is `true` | Warning |
---
## Page-Level
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | | Document title | Non-layout pages call `setDocumentTitle(getMessage('...'))` in `firstUpdated()` (WCAG 2.4.2) | Error | | Document title util | `utils/document-title.js` exists, exports `setDocumentTitle`, SSR-safe (`typeof document` guard) | Error |
---
## Internationalization
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Client i18n | All template strings use `i18n.getMessage()` | Error | | Server i18n | User-facing strings use `gs.getMessage()` | Error | | No hardcoded text | No English strings in templates | Error | | Import | `i18n` imported from `@servicenow/aiux-services` | Error | | Client catch i18n | Client `catch` blocks assign `i18n.getMessage(...)` to `_error` — not raw `e.message` | Error |
---
## SSR Safety
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Constructor guard | No `window`/`document`/`navigator` in constructor | Error | | Render guard | No browser APIs in `render()` | Error | | Loader guard | `isServer` check when using browser APIs | Error | | connectedCallback guard | Browser APIs guarded with `!isServer` | Error | | Event handler safe | No `isServer` needed | Info |
---
## Styling
| Rule | Check | Severity | | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Host display | `:host { display: block }` (or `contents` for list pages) | Error | | No hardcoded colors | No hex/rgb/named colors in templates | Warning | | CSS custom properties | Colors use `var(--color-*)` | Warning | | DaisyUI prefix | All DaisyUI classes use `aiux-` prefix | Warning | | Card wrapper | Widget root is `aiux-card` + `aiux-card-body`, not a raw `<div>` | Warning | | Card background | Cards use `bg-base-100 shadow-sm` | Info | | No inline SVG | Using `<aiux-icon>` | Warning | | Text overflow | Dynamic/prop-driven text has `overflow-wrap: break-word; word-break: break-word; max-width: 100%` — legible at 320px | Warning |
---
## Events
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Namespace | Custom events use `namespace:action` format | Warning | | Bubbling | `bubbles: true, composed: true` | Error | | No self-mutation | `@property()` values not self-assigned | Error | | Bound handlers | Event handlers bound in constructor | Warning | | No arrow in loops | `.map()` uses data attributes, not arrow closures | Warning | | Action guard | Event handlers that call `server.get()` use a boolean flag (e.g. `_actioning`) to prevent overlapping requests | Warning |
---
## Cleanup
| Rule | Check | Severity | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Listeners | Every `addEventListener` has `removeEventListener` | Error | | Observers | Every observer has `.disconnect()` | Error | | Timers | Every `setTimeout`/`setInterval` is cleared | Error | | Record watcher | Subscription has `.unsubscribe()` | Error | | Scoped context | `unprovide(this)` in `disconnectedCallback` | Error | | AbortController | `.abort()` in cleanup | Warning |
---
## Observability
| Rule | Check | Severity | | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------- | | No console in backend | No `console.*` in server files | Error | | No console.warn/error in browser | New `console.warn`/`console.error` flagged | Warning | | Structured logging | `createLogger` (server) / `getLogger` (browser) | Info |
---
## Accessibility
**Invoke the `accessibility` skill now** if any of the following apply to the component or widget being validated:
| Condition | Invoke `accessibility` skill? | | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | | Component has buttons, inputs, links, or any clickable element | Yes — always | | Component renders a modal, dialog, drawer, or overlay | Yes — always | | Component has tabs, menus, dropdowns, or disclosure patterns | Yes — always | | Component uses drag-and-drop or resizable panels | Yes — always | | Component renders dynamic or async-updated content | Yes — always | | Component is a layout, page, or navigation shell | Yes — always | | Component is purely static display with no interaction | Yes — reflow and forced-colors still apply |
> There is no case where `accessibility` is skipped. The conditions above are listed to help identify *which reference files* inside the skill to load — not to gate whether the skill is invoked.
After the `accessibility` skill has been applied, run these minimum checks:
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Keyboard access | All interactive elements reachable and operable via keyboard | Error | | ARIA labels | Icon-only buttons and controls have `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | Error | | Form labels | Every form input has an associated `<label>` or `aria-label` | Error | | Live regions | Async-updated regions have `aria-live="polite"` or `role="status"` | Error | | Reflow 320px | No horizontal scroll at 320px viewport width (WCAG 1.4.10) | Error | | Forced-colors | Interactive, field, and container components have `@media (forced-colors: active)` CSS | Error |
---
## Chat Integration
| Rule | Check | Severity | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Mixin | Chat widgets use `withWidgetContext(AIUXElement)` | Error | | No arrow functions | `client_tools.definition` is regular function | Error | | Context push | `setAiContext()` called with serializable data | Warning |
=== FILE: references/quality/best-practices-checklist.md === # Best Practices Checklist
All 48 principles grouped by category. Validate every implementation against this list.
---
## Widget Core (P1–P25)
- [ ] **P1** Extend `AIUXWidgetElement` — never plain `LitElement` - [ ] **P2** `i18n.getMessage()` for all user-facing text - [ ] **P3** `state: true` for internal state properties - [ ] **P4** All properties initialized in `constructor()` - [ ] **P5** Data fetch in `connectedCallback()` after `super.connectedCallback()` - [ ] **P6** Cleanup in `disconnectedCallback()` — listeners, watchers, timers - [ ] **P7** `_renderX()` helper methods for complex templates - [ ] **P8** `height: 100%` on `:host` and container - [ ] **P9** CSS custom properties for all colors - [ ] **P10** Loading, error, empty, data states all handled - [ ] **P11** `@discoverable(true)` on every widget - [ ] **P12** `<aiux-icon>` for icons — no inline SVG - [ ] **P13** Widget heading: `text-sm font-medium text-text-secondary` - [ ] **P14** `<fade-scroll>` for scrollable lists - [ ] **P15** `this.trackEvent()` for key user actions - [ ] **P16** GlideQuery `.select()` used when column restriction is needed (GlideRecord fetches all columns — switch to GlideQuery to restrict) - [ ] **P17** `setLimit()` on every GlideRecord query - [ ] **P18** `canRead()`/`canWrite()` after `.get()` - [ ] **P19** Validate and coerce all `input.*` parameters - [ ] **P20** Error shape: `data.isError` + `data.errorMessage` - [ ] **P21** No orphan `data.*` fields — client ↔ server aligned - [ ] **P22** `gs.getMessage()` for server-side user strings - [ ] **P23** In-flight request guard (`this._fetching`) - [ ] **P24** Property `type` in every `static properties` entry - [ ] **P25** Reactive state triggers re-render — no manual `this.update()`
---
## Lit Patterns (P26–P33)
- [ ] **P26** `classMap` for conditional classes - [ ] **P27** No `nothing` in attribute positions - [ ] **P28** No self-mutation of `@property()` values - [ ] **P29** Namespace-scoped events: `bubbles: true, composed: true` - [ ] **P30** No anonymous arrow handlers in `.map()` loops - [ ] **P31** `<details>/<summary>` for collapse — not DaisyUI input hack - [ ] **P32** Tooltip directive — not `data-tip` - [ ] **P33** Cards use `bg-base-100 shadow-sm` (elevated) or `bg-base-100 border border-base-300` (bordered)
---
## Performance & Cleanup (P34–P36)
- [ ] **P34** Resource cleanup in `disconnectedCallback` — observers, listeners, timers, AbortControllers - [ ] **P35** No `await` on fire-and-forget — fire and `.catch()` - [ ] **P36** `lazyImage` directive for `<img>` elements
---
## Chat Integration (P37–P39)
- [ ] **P37** `withWidgetContext(AIUXElement)` for chat-integrated widgets - [ ] **P38** `client_tools` definitions use regular functions (not arrows) - [ ] **P39** `setAiContext()` pushes serializable state to chat
---
## Observability (P40–P41)
- [ ] **P40** `createLogger` (server) / `getLogger` (browser) — no `console.*` - [ ] **P41** Correct severity: `debug` per-request, `info` lifecycle, `warn` degraded, `error` failures

## App-Level (P42–P43)

## Common Error Fixes
### "SyntaxError: Unexpected token"
Check bundler output for invalid identifiers from relative imports.
### "this.server is undefined"
Not extending `AIUXWidgetElement`. Widgets MUST extend `AIUXWidgetElement`, not `AIUXElement`.
### "this is undefined in client_tools"
Arrow function in `client_tools.definition`. Use regular function.
### Data not loading
1. Add `gs.info()` in server script to trace execution 2. Check browser console for network errors 3. Verify action name matches between client and server 4. Check parameter priority: `input > options > default`
### Component not rendering
1. Check browser console for errors 2. Verify `@customElement` decorator present with unique tag name 3. Ensure `render()` returns `html` template 4. Check all properties initialized in constructor
### Styles not applying
1. Verify CSS is in `` static styles = css`...` `` block 2. Check DaisyUI classes have `aiux-` prefix 3. Ensure `:host` has `display: block` 4. Check CSS custom property fallbacks
### Properties not updating UI
1. Verify property is in `static properties` with `type` 2. Check `state: true` for internal state 3. Don't mutate arrays/objects — reassign: `this.items = [...newItems]` 4. Check `updated(changedProperties)` logic
### Server script returns empty data
1. Check `gs.info()` logs in System Logs 2. Verify GlideRecord table name is correct 3. Confirm `gr.query()` is called 4. Check ACLs — user may not have access 5. Try `GlideRecordSecure` — it silently filters inaccessible records
### Event listeners not firing
1. Handlers bound in constructor? 2. Using `@event` syntax in templates (not `onevent`)? 3. Custom events have `composed: true` to cross shadow DOM?
### Memory leaks
1. `disconnectedCallback()` with `super.disconnectedCallback()`? 2. All `window`/`document` listeners removed? 3. Record watchers unsubscribed? 4. Intervals/timeouts cleared?
### Context stale after navigation
1. `willUpdate` checking `this.loaderData !== this._prevLoaderData`? 2. Re-calling `provide(this, ...)` inside `willUpdate`? 3. `unprovide(this)` in `disconnectedCallback`?
### Build failure
1. Check `pnpm build` output for compilation errors 2. Verify all imports resolve 3. Check `aiux.json` ↔ `package.json` ↔ `now.config.json` alignment 4. Delete `dist/` and rebuild
### Deploy failure
1. Check `.bin/deploy-full` output 2. Clear instance cache 3. Verify scope matches across config files 4. Check role/ACL XML in `fluent/update/`

# Pages Cookbook

Patterns for page templates in AIUX applications. All examples work in both JS and TS.

---

## Root Layout (`pages/layout.js`)

Apps using the Polaris sidebar/header shell extend `NavLayout` from `@servicenow/aiux-components-nav` and use `navLayoutContext` to drive the sidebar. Apps that do not need the shell (embedded experiences, lightweight prototypes) extend `AIUXAppLayoutElement` directly.

```js
import {NavLayout, navLayoutContext} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-nav';
import {css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {MyAppTheme} from '../theme.js';

@customElement('my-app-layout')
export default class MyAppLayout extends NavLayout {
  static appTheme = MyAppTheme;

  static styles = [
    ...NavLayout.styles,
    css`
      :host {
        --nav-sidebar-bg: linear-gradient(to bottom, #032d42 0%, #044355 100%);
        --nav-layout-bg: #f5f7fa;
      }
    `
  ];

  static async loader(ctx) {
    await super.loader(ctx, {
      appName: 'My App',
      features: {
        menus: false,
        logo: true,
        userSession: true,
        concoursePicker: false
      }
    });

    const pagePath = ctx.pagePath;

    const items = [
      {icon: 'home', title: 'Home', action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/home'}},
      {
        icon: 'list-outline',
        title: 'Incidents',
        action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/list/incident'}
      }
    ];

    navLayoutContext.set({
      ...navLayoutContext.get(),
      items: items.map(item => {
        const isActive = pagePath?.startsWith(item.action?.path);
        return {...item, ...(isActive && {active: true})};
      })
    });
  }
}
```

---

## Generic List Page (`pages/list/[table]/page.js`)

Uses `ListDataManager` for data and `aiux-list-connected` for rendering. Works with any ServiceNow table.

**Critical — `display: contents`:** The page host MUST be `display: contents` so `aiux-list-connected`'s internal flex layout inherits the NavLayout height chain. Using `display: block` breaks the layout — the list collapses and row affordances render in a detached column.

**Critical — bind `aiux-list-connected:*` events, not `aiux-list:*`:** Row/link clicks come through `@aiux-list-connected:reference-link-clicked` and UI actions through `@aiux-list-connected:ui-action-clicked`. These are the stable public API. The inner `aiux-list:*` events (e.g. `aiux-list:cell-link-clicked`) are internal and can change without notice.

```js
import '@servicenow/aiux-components-list';
import {ListDataManager} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-list';
import {AIUXElement} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
import {html, css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {navigate} from '@servicenow/aiux-client';
import {setDocumentTitle} from '../../utils/document-title.js';
import {getMessage} from '../../utils/i18n.js';

@customElement('my-app-list-page')
export default class ListPage extends AIUXElement {
  // REQUIRED: display:contents
  static styles = css`
    :host {
      display: contents;
    }
  `;

  firstUpdated() {
    setDocumentTitle(getMessage('Incidents'));
  }

  static async loader(ctx) {
    const {table} = ctx.params;
    const query = ctx.query?.sysparm_query || '';
    const data = await ListDataManager.fetch({table, query});
    return {table, query, data};
  }

  _handleRowClick(e) {
    const {referenceTable, referenceSysId, listTable, listSysId} = e.detail;
    const table = referenceTable || listTable;
    const sysId = referenceSysId || listSysId;
    if (table && sysId) navigate(`/record/${table}/${sysId}`);
  }

  _handleUIAction(e) {
    const {uiAction, table} = e.detail || {};
    if (uiAction?.name === 'new_record' && table) {
      navigate(`/record/${table}/-1`);
    }
  }

  render() {
    const {data, table, query} = this.loaderData || {};
    return html`
      <aiux-list-connected
        table=${table}
        .query=${query || ''}
        .data=${data}
        @aiux-list-connected:reference-link-clicked=${this._handleRowClick}
        @aiux-list-connected:ui-action-clicked=${this._handleUIAction}
      ></aiux-list-connected>
    `;
  }
}
```

## Generic Record Page (`pages/record/[table]/[id]/page.js`)

Uses `RecordDataManager` and `aiux-record-provider`. `sysId="-1"` opens a new-record form.

**Critical — `onOpenRecord` is a property callback**, not a DOM event. Use `.onOpenRecord=${fn}` (dot-binding). The handler receives `(table, sysId)` as separate arguments, not a `CustomEvent`. Using `@onOpenRecord` silently does nothing.

```js
import '@servicenow/aiux-components-record';
import {RecordDataManager} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-record';
import {AIUXElement, getLogger} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
import {html, css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {navigate} from '@servicenow/aiux-client';
import {setDocumentTitle} from '../../utils/document-title.js';
import {getMessage} from '../../utils/i18n.js';

const log = getLogger('my-app-record-page');

@customElement('my-app-record-page')
export default class RecordPage extends AIUXElement {
  static styles = css`
    :host {
      display: block;
      height: 100%;
    }
  `;

  firstUpdated() {
    const {table, id} = this.loaderData || {};
    setDocumentTitle(getMessage(table || 'Record'));
  }

  static async loader(ctx) {
    const {table, id} = ctx.params;
    let rawData = null;
    if (table && id && id !== '-1') {
      try {
        rawData = await RecordDataManager.fetchRecord({table, sysId: id});
      } catch (e) {
        log.error({error: e.message}, 'Failed to fetch record');
      }
    }
    return {table, id, rawData};
  }

  _handleOpenRecord(table, sysId) {
    if (table && sysId) navigate(`/record/${table}/${sysId}`);
  }

  render() {
    const {rawData, table, id} = this.loaderData || {};
    return html`
      <aiux-record-provider
        .data=${rawData}
        table=${table || ''}
        sysId=${id || ''}
        show-error-details="true"
        .onOpenRecord=${this._handleOpenRecord}
      >
        <aiux-record-form></aiux-record-form>
      </aiux-record-provider>
    `;
  }
}
```

**Troubleshooting — "Error loading record":** Keep `show-error-details="true"` to see the real error. Common causes:

- Invalid or empty `sysId`
- Instance GraphQL schema older than the package version (instance/build mismatch, not an app bug)

## Nested Layout (`pages/[table]/[id]/layout.js`)

For route groups that need shared data via scoped context. The `willUpdate` hook is **required** — without it, navigating between records under the same layout updates `loaderData` but never re-runs `provide()`, leaving child pages with stale data.

```js
import {AIUXElement} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
import {html} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {detailContext} from '../../../contexts/detail-context.js';

@customElement('my-app-detail-layout')
export default class DetailLayout extends AIUXElement {
  _prevLoaderData = null;

  static async loader(ctx) {
    const {id} = ctx.params;
    return {id, record: await fetchRecord(id)};
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback();
    const {id, record} = this.loaderData || {};
    detailContext.provide(this, {id, record});
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    super.disconnectedCallback();
    detailContext.unprovide(this); // REQUIRED — prevents memory leaks
  }

  willUpdate() {
    if (this.loaderData !== this._prevLoaderData) {
      this._prevLoaderData = this.loaderData;
      const {id, record} = this.loaderData || {};
      detailContext.provide(this, {id, record});
    }
  }

  render() {
    return html`<slot></slot>`;
  }
}
```

Child pages consume:

```js
static contexts = [detailContext];
render() {
  const {id, record} = detailContext.get(this) || {};
}
```

import {html, css} from 'lit';

  static styles = css`
    :host {
      display: block;

# Navigation Patterns

## `application.js` — The Preferred App Shell Pattern

Production apps (e.g. AICT) use `application.js` as the lifecycle module instead of a custom `NavLayout` class. The framework calls `setup()` once per SSR request before loaders run. Nav items, features, and app title are set via `navLayoutContext` inside `setup()`. The app shell is `aiux-nav-layout` (declared via `applicationLayout` in `application.js`).

```js
// application.js
import {navLayoutContext} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-nav';
import {i18n} from '@servicenow/aiux-services';
import {
  isPluginActive,
  getSystemProperty
} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
import {MY_THEME} from './theme.js';
import {
  licenseContext,
  setLicenseContext,
  fetchLicense
} from './contexts/license-context.js';

export default {
  appTheme: MY_THEME,
  applicationLayout: 'aiux-nav-layout', // use platform nav shell
  contexts: [licenseContext], // auto-fetched before setup()

  async setup(ctx) {
    const [licenseResult] = await Promise.all([fetchLicense(ctx)]);
    setLicenseContext(licenseResult ?? {hasEnterpriseLicense: false});
    const hasEnterpriseLicense = licenseResult?.hasEnterpriseLicense === true;

    const features = {
      menus: false,
      logo: true,
      userSession: false,
      profile: true,
      chat: ctx.chat?.enabled === true,
      announcements: true,
      helpPanel: true
    };

    const items = [
      {
        icon: 'home',
        title: i18n.getMessage('Home'),
        action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/home'}
      },
      {
        icon: 'list-outline',
        title: i18n.getMessage('Inventory'),
        action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/inventory'},
        activePath: '/inventory'
      },
      ...(hasEnterpriseLicense
        ? [
            {
              icon: 'lightbulb',
              title: i18n.getMessage('Insights'),
              action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/insights'}
            }
          ]
        : []),
      {
        icon: 'gear',
        title: i18n.getMessage('Settings'),
        l2Nav: [
          {
            title: i18n.getMessage('Users'),
            action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/settings/users'}
          },
          {
            title: i18n.getMessage('Integrations'),
            action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/settings/integrations'}
          }
        ]
      }
    ];

    const current = navLayoutContext.get();
    navLayoutContext.set({
      ...current,
      appTitle: i18n.getMessage('My App'),
      features,
      items,
      defaultLogoFull:
        getSystemProperty('com.glide.myapp.logo_full') || 'servicenow',
      defaultLogoIcon:
        getSystemProperty('com.glide.myapp.logo_small') || 'servicenow'
    });
  },

  // Rewrite legacy SN URLs to app routes before navigation commits
  navigate(navCtx) {
    // navCtx.toAppPath, navCtx.to (URL), navCtx.from (URL)
    // return a new path string to redirect, or undefined to allow through
    if (/^\/incident\.do$/.test(navCtx.toAppPath)) {
      const sysId = navCtx.to.searchParams.get('sys_id');
      if (sysId) return `/record/incident/${sysId}`;
    }
    return undefined;
  },

  // Clean up nav when leaving this app (CSR cross-app navigation)
  teardown() {
    navLayoutContext.set({
      items: [],
      defaultLogoFull: null,
      defaultLogoIcon: null
    });
  }
};
```

### L2 Nav (Sub-menus) and L3 Nav (Header Tabs)

```js
// L2 (sidebar sub-menu items)
{
  icon: 'building',
  title: i18n.getMessage('Govern'),
  l2Nav: [
    {title: i18n.getMessage('Risk'), action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/control/risk'}},
    {title: i18n.getMessage('Security'), action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/security'}, l3Nav: [
      {label: i18n.getMessage('Overview'), path: '/security/overview'},
      {label: i18n.getMessage('Events'), path: '/security/events'}
    ]}
  ]
}

// activePath — marks an item active when any child route matches
{icon: 'inventory', title: 'Inventory', action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/inventory/all'}, activePath: '/inventory'}
```

### `setHeaderConfig` and `setPageActions` (from nested layouts)

Nested layouts can push dynamic header config and action buttons to the nav shell:

```js
import {setHeaderConfig, setPageActions} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-nav';

// In a nested layout's connectedCallback or willUpdate
setHeaderConfig(this, {
  actionsDropdown: true,
  title: assetName,
  metadata: [
    {label: 'Active', iconName: 'check-outline', iconClass: 'text-success'}
  ],
  l3: [
    {label: i18n.getMessage('Overview'), path: `/inventory/${id}`},
    {label: i18n.getMessage('Details'), path: `/inventory/${id}/details`}
  ]
});

setPageActions(this, [
  {
    id: 'manage_asset',
    label: i18n.getMessage('Manage'),
    handler: async () => {
      await manageAsset(id);
      await this._refreshAfterAction();
    }
  },
  {
    id: 'unmanage_asset',
    label: i18n.getMessage('Unmanage'),
    handler: async () => {
      await unmanageAsset(id);
    }
  }
]);
```

## NavLayout — The Simple App Shell (Polaris-shell apps only)

Apps using the Polaris sidebar/header shell extend `NavLayout` from `@servicenow/aiux-components-nav`. It provides the sidebar, header, user session, and content slot. Apps that do not need the Polaris shell (embedded experiences, lightweight prototypes) extend `AIUXAppLayoutElement` directly.

```js
import {NavLayout, navLayoutContext} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-nav';
import {css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {MyAppTheme} from '../theme.js';

@customElement('my-app-layout')
export default class MyAppLayout extends NavLayout {
  static appTheme = MyAppTheme;

  static styles = [
    ...NavLayout.styles,
    css`
      :host {
        --nav-sidebar-bg: linear-gradient(to bottom, #032d42 0%, #044355 100%);
        --nav-layout-bg: #f5f7fa;
      }
    `
  ];

  static async loader(ctx) {
    await super.loader(ctx, {
      appName: 'My App',
      features: {
        menus: false,
        logo: true,
        userSession: true,
        concoursePicker: false
      }
    });
    // configure sidebar items (see Sidebar section below)
  }
}
```

### Key Rules

- **Polaris-shell root layout extends `NavLayout`** — non-shell apps extend `AIUXAppLayoutElement`. Nested layouts extend `AIUXElement`.
- **Always call `super.loader(ctx, options)`** before setting sidebar items
- **Always spread `...NavLayout.styles`** in `static styles` — omitting it breaks the shell
- **Pages inside NavLayout MUST use `display: contents`** on `:host` — otherwise `aiux-list-connected` and other flex children collapse

### Features Object

| Feature           | Type    | Description                                  |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `appName`         | string  | Display name in header                       |
| `menus`           | boolean | Show app menus (default: false)              |
| `logo`            | boolean | Show ServiceNow logo (default: true)         |
| `userSession`     | boolean | Show user avatar/session (default: true)     |
| `concoursePicker` | boolean | Show concourse scope picker (default: false) |

### CSS Custom Properties

| Property              | Default | Description                            |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `--nav-sidebar-bg`    | —       | Sidebar background (gradient or color) |
| `--nav-layout-bg`     | —       | Main content area background           |
| `--nav-sidebar-width` | —       | Sidebar width when expanded            |

### navLayoutContext

`navLayoutContext` is the shared context for sidebar state. Always read-modify-write:

```js
navLayoutContext.set({
  ...navLayoutContext.get(),
  items: [...],        // sidebar items
  // other props the context supports
});
```

---

## File-Based Routing

Pages live in `pages/`. Folders map directly to URL segments. `[param]` brackets create dynamic segments.

| File path                           | Route                | Params                              |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `pages/home/page.js`                | `/home`              | —                                   |
| `pages/list/[table]/page.js`        | `/list/:table`       | `ctx.params.table`                  |
| `pages/record/[table]/[id]/page.js` | `/record/:table/:id` | `ctx.params.table`, `ctx.params.id` |
| `pages/[...slug]/page.js`           | `/:slug*`            | `ctx.params.slug` (catch-all)       |

Catch-all segments use `[...name]` to match the remainder of the path.

---

## Programmatic Navigation

```js
import {navigate} from '@servicenow/aiux-client';

// App-relative path — the router prepends basePath automatically
navigate('/record/incident/abc123');

// Replace current history entry (redirect-style)
navigate('/home', {replace: true});
```

The path is **app-relative** — do NOT include `basePath`.

---

## Anchor Links

Anchor links require the **full basePath-prefixed** href. Read `basePath` from the loader `ctx`.

```js
static async loader(ctx) {
  return {basePath: ctx.basePath};
}

render() {
  const {basePath} = this.loaderData || {};
  return html`<a href="${basePath}/home">Home</a>`;
}
```

**Do NOT use relative hrefs** like `./home` — they do not resolve correctly. The router intercepts absolute `basePath`-prefixed links for SPA navigation.

---

## Sidebar Navigation Items

Sidebar items are configured in the root layout's `loader` via `navLayoutContext`:

```js
const items = [
  {icon: 'home', title: 'Home', action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/home'}},
  {
    icon: 'list-outline',
    title: 'Incidents',
    action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/list/incident'}
  },
  {
    icon: 'document-outline',
    title: 'Tasks',
    action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/list/task'}
  },
  // Divider
  {divider: true},
  // External link
  {
    icon: 'link-outline',
    title: 'Docs',
    action: {type: 'link', href: 'https://docs.servicenow.com'}
  }
];
```

### Item Shape

| Property      | Type                     | Description                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `icon`        | string                   | Icon name for `<aiux-icon>`        |
| `title`       | string                   | Display text                       |
| `action.type` | `'navigate'` or `'link'` | Navigation type                    |
| `action.path` | string                   | App-relative path (for `navigate`) |
| `action.href` | string                   | Full URL (for `link`)              |
| `active`      | boolean                  | Highlight as current               |
| `divider`     | boolean                  | Render as separator                |

### Active State

Set active based on current `pagePath`:

```js
static async loader(ctx) {
  const pagePath = ctx.pagePath;
  // ...
  navLayoutContext.set({
    ...navLayoutContext.get(),
    items: items.map(item => {
      const isActive = pagePath?.startsWith(item.action?.path);
      return {...item, ...(isActive && {active: true})};
    })
  });
}
```

---

## Layout Chain

The layout chain resolves from outermost (root) to innermost:

```
pages/layout.js           → Root layout (NavLayout, sidebar, theme)
  pages/detail/layout.js  → Nested layout (scoped context provider)
    pages/detail/[id].js  → Page (consumes context)
```

Each layout's loader runs **before** the page's loader. Layouts render their content via `<slot></slot>`.

Scoped AIUX applications add ServiceNow metadata (tables, roles, ACLs, navigation) and a deploy pipeline via the Fluent SDK.

## Fluent SDK File Map

```
fluent/
├── update/
│   ├── sys_db_object/           # Table definitions
│   ├── sys_dictionary/          # Field definitions
│   ├── sys_user_role/           # Roles
│   ├── sys_security_acl/        # ACLs
│   ├── sys_app_module/          # Application navigation modules
│   └── sys_ai_agent/            # AI agent configurations (optional)
└── now.config.json              # Scope and scopeId
```

---

## Build & Deploy Pipeline

```bash
pnpm run build                  # Build the AIUX app
pnpm run deploy                 # Deploy to ServiceNow instance
pnpm run deploy:full            # Build + deploy in one step
```

`deploy:full` runs:

1. `pnpm build` — compiles app, generates widget XML
2. `pnpm deploy` — pushes to instance via Fluent SDK

---

## Common Gotchas

| Issue                            | Cause                                                           | Fix                                              |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Deploy fails with scope mismatch | `now.config.json`, `aiux.json`, `fluent/` have different scopes | Align all three                                  |
| Stale metadata on instance       | Cached old version                                              | Clear instance cache, re-deploy                  |
| Missing type definitions         | `dist/app` out of sync                                          | Delete `dist/`, rebuild                          |
| "Record not found" after deploy  | Role/ACL not deployed                                           | Check `sys_user_role` and `sys_security_acl` XML |
| Widget not visible on instance   | Missing `@discoverable(true)`                                   | Add decorator and rebuild                        |

Three files must agree for a role-protected resource:

1. **`sys_user_role/`** — role definition XML
2. **`sys_security_acl/`** — ACL referencing the role
3. **Application code** — role checks in server scripts (`GlideRecordSecure`, `gs.hasRole()`)

# Adding Extensions to an Existing App

Use this reference when the user's intent is to **overlay pages onto a host application** rather than add a page to the current standalone app. Extensions live in `src/extensions/` and do not modify host application code. This reference is self-contained — no companion skill needs to be invoked for extension work.

## When This Applies

- User says "add an extension page", "extend `<host app>`", "overlay a page on `<host>`", "create an extension for `<host-scope>`"
- The target route belongs to a **different, existing host experience** — not a page under this app's own `pages/` directory
- Distinguish from a normal BUILD-mode page: a normal page lives at `pages/<route>/page.js` in *this* app; an extension page lives at `src/extensions/<host-scope>/<host-basename>/pages/<route>/page.js` (or `src/extensions/<experience-sys_id>/pages/<route>/page.js`) and targets a *host* app.

## Scaffolding Options

**Option A — Scaffold a new extension project from scratch:**

```bash
npx @servicenow/sdk@latest init --template javascript.aiux-extension
```

This scaffolds a complete extension project with `src/extensions/`, `application.js`, a hello-world page, and `now.config.json` pre-configured.

**Option B — Add extensions to an existing AIUX application:**

If you already have a working AIUX app and want it to extend another host experience, no re-scaffold is needed. Just:

1. Create the `src/extensions/<host-scope>/<host-basename>/pages/<route>/page.js` directory structure
2. Optionally add a per-host lifecycle module at `src/extensions/<host-scope>/<host-basename>/application.js` for nav contributions
3. Build and deploy as normal — `pnpm build && pnpm run deploy`

The build auto-discovers `src/extensions/` pages and emits the host-targeting records alongside your app's own pages. **Caution:** combining your own `pages/` with `src/extensions/` pages in the same project is unsafe — see the extensibility doc's Known Limitations.

## Path Conventions

Two equivalent formats — both are discovered identically. A single project can mix conventions across hosts.

**Convention 1 (scope + basename — familiar):**

```
src/extensions/<host-scope>/<host-basename>/pages/<route>/page.js
src/extensions/sn_app_aict_ui/aict/pages/home/page.js
```

**Convention 2 (direct sys_id — explicit):**

```
src/extensions/<experience-sys_id>/pages/<route>/page.js
src/extensions/2f86ed94fdab96a806bbbb5b8573c5d5/pages/home/page.js
```

**Key:** extension pages use `page.js` (not `index.js`). The route is derived from the directory path, not the filename.

If the host scope/basename/sys_id is unknown and cannot be inferred from the workspace (e.g. an existing `src/extensions/` sibling), ask the user before scaffolding.

## Key Concepts

- **Pages = Lit web components** extending `AIUXElement`
- **Loaders = SSR data fetching** via `static async loader(ctx)`
- **Layouts = nested inheritance** with per-level most-specific-wins precedence
- **Extensions = overlay pages** on host applications without modifying host code
- **Host-level chrome** (nav items, etc.) is contributed via `application.js` exporting `setup(ctx)` — `extension.js` is not read by the build

## Extension Page Template

```js
import {html, css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {
  AIUXElement,
  decorators,
  getLogger
} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-core';
import {i18n} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-services';

const {roles} = decorators;
const log = getLogger('{{TAG_NAME}}');

// Save to: src/extensions/<host-scope>/<host-basename>/pages/<route>/page.js

@customElement('x-scope-page-name') // Replace 'x-scope' with your scope prefix
// @roles(['admin', 'user'])  // Uncomment to restrict access to roles
export default class MyPage extends AIUXElement {
  static styles = css`
    :host { display: block; height: 100%; }
  `;

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._loading = false;
    this._error = null;
  }

  /**
   * Runs on the server during initial render and on the client during
   * navigation. Returned object is embedded as __LOADER_DATA__ and
   * exposed as this.loaderData in render().
   */
  static async loader(ctx) {
    try {
      return {pageTitle: i18n.getMessage('{{PAGE_TITLE}}')};
    } catch (err) {
      log.error({error: err.message}, '{{CLASS_NAME}} loader error');
      throw err;
    }
  }

  render() {
    if (!this.loaderData) {
      return html`<p>${i18n.getMessage('Loading')}</p>`;
    }
    if (this.loaderData.error) {
      return html`<p>${this.loaderData.error}</p>`;
    }
    return html`<h1>${this.loaderData.pageTitle}</h1>`;
  }
}
```

Never use browser APIs (`window`, `document`, `localStorage`) inside `render()` or `loader()` — both run during SSR. Guard with `isServer` per `references/foundation/ssr-safety.md`.

## Loader Module Pattern (optional separate file)

```js
// Location: src/extensions/<host>/pages/<route>/loaders/data.js
import {getHeaders, getLogger} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-core';

const log = getLogger('fetchPageData');

export async function fetchPageData(ctx) {
  try {
    const url = new URL(`${ctx.protocol}://${ctx.hostname}/api/v2/your-endpoint`);
    if (ctx.params.id) url.searchParams.set('id', ctx.params.id);

    const resp = await fetch(url.toString(), {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: getHeaders(ctx),
      credentials: 'include'
    });
    if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`Failed to fetch data: ${resp.status} ${resp.statusText}`);
    return await resp.json();
  } catch (err) {
    log.error({error: err.message}, 'fetchPageData error');
    throw err;
  }
}
```

Import it in the page: `static async loader(ctx) { return {pageTitle: '...', data: await fetchPageData(ctx)}; }`

## Layout Override Pattern

Nested layout precedence (highest to lowest):

1. Extension layout at this level
2. Extension layout at parent level (inherited)
3. Host layout at this level
4. Host layout at parent level (inherited)
5. Default layout from core-ui

If no `layout.js` is defined at a level, the extension inherits the host's layout at that level automatically.

```js
// Location: src/extensions/<extension>/pages/<route>/layout.js
import {html} from 'lit';
import {NavLayout} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-nav';

export default class MyLayoutOverride extends NavLayout {
  render() {
    // Option 1: use host layout as-is — return super.render();
    // Option 2: wrap/customize while keeping structure
    return html`<div class="extension-layout">${super.render()}</div>`;
    // Option 3: fully custom layout — must still render <slot> for the child page
  }

  // Override specific regions instead of the whole layout:
  // _renderSidebar() / _renderToolbar() / _renderHeader() / _renderContent()
}
```

**Example:** host defines `layout.js` at `measure/` (L2) and `measure/value/` (L3). Extension defines `layout.js` only at `measure/` (L2). At `/measure/value`: extension L2 layout applies (most-specific), host L3 layout is inherited (no extension override at that level).

## Continue in This Skill

After scaffolding the extension page/loader/layout, run through the normal pipeline for anything the templates above don't cover:

- **Styling** — `references/design/daisyui-patterns.md`, `references/design/css-custom-properties.md`
- **Accessibility** — invoke `accessibility` companion skill (required — extension pages render real UI and must comply with WCAG 2.2 AA)
- **i18n** — invoke `internationalization` companion skill (required — all page/loader strings must use `i18n.getMessage()`, never hardcoded English)
- **UI discovery** — invoke `ui-discovery` before writing any custom UI inside the extension page

## Key Differences From Standalone Pages

| Aspect | Standalone page (this app) | Extension page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Location | `pages/<route>/page.js` | `src/extensions/<host>/pages/<route>/page.js` |
| Filename | `page.js` | `page.js` (route from directory path, not filename) |
| Layout | `pages/layout.js` or `application.js` | Nested layout override, most-specific-wins |
| Modifies host code | N/A | Never — overlay only |
| Nav wiring | `application.js` setup() / `pages/layout.js` loader | Host-level chrome via `application.js` `setup(ctx)` |

export default {

  setup(ctx) {
    const items = [
      {
        icon: 'home',
        title: i18n.getMessage('My App'),
        action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/home'}
      },
      {
        icon: 'list',
        title: i18n.getMessage('Incidents'),
        action: {type: 'navigate', path: '/incidents'}
      }
    ];

    const activeRoute = ctx.app?.routes?.find(r => r.active);
    const itemsWithActive = items.map(item => ({
      ...item,
      ...(item.action?.path === activeRoute?.route && {active: true})
    }));

    const current = navLayoutContext.get();
    navLayoutContext.set({
      ...current,
      appTitle: i18n.getMessage('My App'),
      features: {
        menus: false,
        logo: true,
        userSession: false,
        notifications: false,
        themeToggle: false,
        densityPicker: false,
        unifiedExperience: false,
        profile: true,
        helpPanel: true
      },
      items: itemsWithActive,
      defaultLogoFull: 'servicenow',
      defaultLogoIcon: 'servicenow'
    });
  },

  teardown() {
    navLayoutContext.set({
      items: [],
      defaultLogoFull: null,
      defaultLogoIcon: null
    });

Output for Lux requests must be a Lux app: aiux.json, application.js, theme.js, pages/<route>/page.js, plus Fluent (*.now.ts) for tables, ACLs and REST APIs. Never produce React UI Pages for Lux requests. Before writing code, invoke lux-app-method (how to split a full app between Studio and a local Lux build), then these companion skills by name: lux-ref-app (project scaffold to copy, pages, navigation, theme), lux-ref-foundation (AIUXElement, Lit, SSR, loaders, data fetching, server scripts), lux-ref-design (DaisyUI, Tailwind, validation, audit). Paths such as references/... in the text below refer to files inside those companion skills.
# AIUX Build
Orchestrator skill for building production-quality AIUX apps. It directs the LLM to the right reference file or companion skill at each decision point.
**Prerequisite:** App scaffold exists — `aiux.json`, `package.json`, `pages/` directory, and either `pages/layout.js` (simple pattern) or `application.js` (production pattern).
---
## Companion Skills — When to Invoke
These skills must be invoked at the exact moments listed. They are not optional.
| Skill | Invoke when | What it provides | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ui-discovery` | **Before writing any UI code** — every BUILD and EDIT task | Unified index of packaged components AND widgets installed on the connected instance. Reuse what it ranks; write custom only when nothing matches. | | `accessibility` | **Every BUILD and EDIT task** — all UI components and pages regardless of apparent interactivity level | WCAG 2.2 AA ARIA patterns, keyboard nav, focus management, live regions, Shadow DOM labeling, reflow, forced-colors | | `internationalization` | Any user-visible string, date, number, currency, or sort operation | Correct `i18n.getMessage()` usage, parameterized messages, ICU plural/select, locale-aware formatting | | `localization` | Adding a new locale, RTL layout, translated catalogs, script/font coverage | Per-locale adaptation on top of the i18n layer (prerequisite: `internationalization` already applied) | | `migrate-header-config` | Migrating `headerConfig.js` per-page files into `application.js` | Post-migration review: stale comments, CSR/SSR behavior changes, scope problems |
**Order of operations for BUILD and EDIT tasks:**
1. `ui-discovery` — rank components and widgets, reuse a match or decide to write custom 2. Write the component/page/widget using this skill's references 3. `accessibility` — wire ARIA, keyboard, focus, reflow, and forced-colors (mandatory — not conditional on presence of interactive elements) 4. `internationalization` — wrap all strings, format all locale-sensitive values
> **EDIT tasks included:** Steps 3–4 apply after every EDIT that touches templates or server scripts — not only on net-new BUILD tasks.
---
## Mode Router
**Step 1 — Classify intent.** Do NOT load references yet.
| User intent | Mode | References to load (after intent is clear) | | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | "Add", "build", "create", "new page/widget/component" | **BUILD** | `app/pages-cookbook.md` + relevant widget refs | | "Add extension", "extend `<host app>`", "overlay page on `<host>`" | **BUILD (extension)** | `app/extensions.md` | | "Change", "update", "edit", "add nav item", "modify" | **EDIT** | `app/navigation-patterns.md`, `app/theme-and-config.md` | | "Not working", "error", "broken", "fix", "debug" | **DEBUG** | `quality/debugging-guide.md`, `quality/validation-rules.md` | | "Review", "audit", "check quality", "analyze" | **ANALYZE** | `quality/audit-checklist.md`, `quality/best-practices-checklist.md` |
**Step 2 — If intent is ambiguous, ask the user to clarify** before loading any references.
**Step 3 — Load only the references listed** for the classified mode. Read each file directly from this skill's `references/` directory (e.g. `references/app/pages-cookbook.md`). Do not load references for other modes.
For BUILD: also invoke `ui-discovery` before loading any other reference.
---
## Project Discovery (always first)
Read these before writing a single line:
1. `aiux.json` — basename, landing page, chat gate 2. `package.json` — dependencies, scripts 3. `theme.js` — color tokens, shape 4. `pages/` directory listing — routing conventions, existing patterns 5. `application.js` or `pages/layout.js` — which app architecture pattern is in use 6. One existing page file — learn the naming and import style the project already uses
---
## App Architecture
Two patterns exist. Detect which one the project uses before writing navigation or layout code.
| Signal | Pattern | Where nav items live | | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------- | | `pages/layout.js` extends `NavLayout` | **Simple** | `pages/layout.js` loader | | `application.js` exports `{ setup, navigate, teardown }` | **Production** | `application.js` `setup()` |
**Simple — `pages/layout.js`:**
```js import {NavLayout, navLayoutContext} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-nav'; @customElement('my-app-layout') export default class MyAppLayout extends NavLayout { static appTheme = MY_THEME; static async loader(ctx) { await super.loader(ctx, {appName: 'My App', features: {logo: true}}); navLayoutContext.set({...navLayoutContext.get(), items: [...]}); } } ```
**Production — `application.js`:**
```js export default { appTheme: MY_THEME, applicationLayout: 'aiux-nav-layout', // required — platform nav shell contexts: [licenseContext], // auto-fetched before setup() async setup(ctx) { navLayoutContext.set({ ...navLayoutContext.get(), appTitle: i18n.getMessage('My App'), features: {logo: true, profile: true, chat: ctx.chat?.enabled === true}, items: [...] }); }, navigate(navCtx) { return undefined; }, teardown() { navLayoutContext.set({items: []}); } }; ```
Page filename: `page.js`.
---
## Placement Conventions
| Artifact | Location | Rule | | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | App lifecycle | `application.js` | `setup()`, `navigate()`, `teardown()`, theme, contexts | | Theme | `theme.js` | Color tokens, shape — imported by `application.js` | | Pages | `pages/<route>/page.js` | File-based routing | | Nested layouts | `pages/<route>/layout.js` | Scoped context providers | | Extension pages | `src/extensions/<host>/pages/<route>/page.js` | Overlay on a different host app — see `references/app/extensions.md` | | Page-scoped components | `pages/<route>/components/` | Used by one page only | | Shared components | `components/` | Used by 2+ pages | | Widgets | `widgets/<name>/index.js` + `server.js` | Self-contained with server script | | Shared loaders | `loaders/` | Fetch functions shared across pages | | Contexts | `contexts/` | `createContext()` definitions | | Constants | `constants/` | Table fields, roles, enums | | Utilities | `utils/` | Formatters, shared helpers | | Document title | `utils/document-title.js` | `setDocumentTitle()` — WCAG 2.4.2 page titles |
---
## BUILD Mode
### Step 0 — UI Discovery (mandatory gate)
Invoke the `ui-discovery` skill before drafting any plan. It is mandatory, not optional. It returns a suggested component or widget, or nothing if none fits.
### Step 1 — Present Plan (mandatory gate)
Once the discovery gate above has run, present a concise plan to the user:
1. **What you understood** — restate the user's request in your own words 2. **What you will build** — list pages, widgets, components, server scripts, and say explicitly whether each is a reused `ui-discovery` match or new custom code, and why 3. **Navigation changes** — new routes, nav items, layout changes 4. **Data sources** — tables, APIs, server script actions 5. **Styling approach** — theme tokens, DaisyUI components, custom CSS
Wait for user confirmation. If the user corrects or refines, update the plan. Only proceed after approval.
### Step 2 — Adding a Page
If the target page overlays a different, existing host application (`src/extensions/...`) rather than this app's own `pages/` directory, load `references/app/extensions.md` instead and follow its steps. Otherwise:
Load: `references/app/pages-cookbook.md`
1. Detect page type: home / list / record / custom / nested-layout 2. Create `pages/<route>/page.js` extending `AIUXElement` 3. Add `static async loader(ctx)` for data — use `Promise.allSettled` for multiple fetches 4. Add `firstUpdated()` calling `setDocumentTitle(getMessage('Page Name'))` — required for every non-layout page (WCAG 2.4.2) 5. Wire navigation in `application.js` setup() or `pages/layout.js` loader 6. Apply `isServer` guards to any browser API in `connectedCallback` 7. If the page renders any configurable widget (has `@configProperty`), add the `aiux-config-id` attribute on each instance — load `references/config-framework/config-id.md`
### Step 3 — Adding a Widget
Load: `references/widget/component-patterns.md`, `references/widget/server-scripts.md`, `references/widget/decorators.md`, `references/widget/data-fetching.md`
1. Create `widgets/<name>/index.js` + `widgets/<name>/server.js` 2. Apply required decorators: `@customElement`, `@discoverable(true)`, `@name`, `@description`, `@bestFor`, `@server` 3. Implement all four render states: loading (skeleton), error, empty, data 4. Server script: IIFE pattern (see below), `GlideRecordSecure`, `setLimit()`, `gs.getMessage()` 5. If widget needs configurable properties: a. Load `references/config-framework/config-field-types.md` — add `@configProperty` decorators b. Load `references/config-framework/config-id.md` — add a static `aiux-config-id` on every instance in host pages (always do this after adding `@configProperty`) c. If fields need accordion grouping → load `references/config-framework/config-groups.md` d. If widget needs config that opens a platform table → load `references/config-framework/config-external.md` e. If fields need conditional visibility → load `references/config-framework/config-depends-on.md` f. If widget links out to an external url/list/table/record for config (**custom-url** mode) or owns its entire bespoke config UI (**inline-auto** / self-config mode) → load `references/config-framework/config-modes.md`
A file is an AIUX widget when it has all four: `export default` class extending `AIUXWidgetElement` + `@discoverable(true)` + `@customElement` + `@bestFor`.
### Step 4 — Styling
Load: `references/design/css-custom-properties.md`, `references/design/daisyui-patterns.md`
All `aiux-` prefixed DaisyUI classes. CSS custom properties with hex fallbacks. `:host` display by page type (see Styling section).
### Step 5 — Accessibility (companion skill — mandatory)
Invoke the `accessibility` skill. This step is **not conditional** — invoke it for every component, page, and widget regardless of whether elements appear explicitly interactive. WCAG 2.2 AA requirements (reflow at 320px, forced-colors, keyboard nav, ARIA landmarks, focus management) apply to all UI output.
### Step 6 — i18n (companion skill)
Invoke `internationalization` skill. Every user-visible string uses `i18n.getMessage()`. Every date/number uses locale-aware formatting.
### Step 7 — Validate
Run through `references/quality/validation-rules.md` and `references/quality/best-practices-checklist.md`. Fix all violations before presenting output.
---
## EDIT Mode
Load: `references/app/navigation-patterns.md`, `references/app/theme-and-config.md`
### Step 0 — UI Discovery (mandatory gate)
Invoke the `ui-discovery` skill before touching any file. It is mandatory, not optional. It returns a suggested component or widget, or nothing if none fits.
### Step 1 — Make the edit
Using what Step 0 returned, decide whether to reuse the match or write custom code — write custom only when nothing fits.
**After editing**, run these steps in order:
1. Re-invoke `accessibility` companion skill — not BUILD-only; catches regressions in any touched template 2. Re-invoke `internationalization` companion skill — catches any newly hardcoded strings 3. Run `references/quality/validation-rules.md` — full assertion pass against the changed component or widget; fix all Error-severity violations before presenting output
| Edit type | Read | Change | Verify | | ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | | Add nav item | `application.js` or `pages/layout.js` | `items[]` array | Active state, route path | | Change theme | `theme.js` | Token values | `appTheme` reference | | Add page route | `pages/` directory | New page file + nav | No route conflicts | | Modify widget data | `widgets/<name>/index.js` + `server.js` | Both files | Action name match, response shape | | Add context sharing | Layout + consumer page | Context definition + provide/consume | `willUpdate` re-provision | | Add/edit `@configProperty` | `config-framework/config-field-types.md` | `@configProperty` decorators on component | `aiux-config-id` on all host instances (`config-id.md`) |

## DEBUG Mode
Load: `references/quality/debugging-guide.md`
| Symptom | Check | Fix | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Blank page | Console errors, loader return | Missing `isServer` guard; loader crash; **non-existent `aiux-components-*` import** (see Module Resolution Traps in `lux-ref-foundation`) | | Widget shows no data | Server script | Must be `(function(data, options, input) { ... })(data, options, input)` | | Widget not rendering | `@customElement` + export | Missing decorator or wrong base class | | Nav shell missing | `application.js` | Add `applicationLayout: 'aiux-nav-layout'` | | Data not loading | Server script action name | Action name in `server.get({action})` must match handler | | Chart/library renders nothing | Module specifier | Dynamic `await import('lib')` does not resolve in browser — use a static import | | Styles not applying | `:host` display, class names | Missing `display: block`; class typo | | Properties not updating | `static properties` declaration | Undeclared reactive property; mutating object without reassignment | | Context always default | Scoped context call | `detailContext.get(this)` — `this` is required | | Loader crashes on error | `Promise.allSettled` | Check `.status === 'fulfilled'` before accessing `.value` | | Client fetch 403/401 | Fetch method | Use `aiuxFetch` — adds XSRF + auth headers | | L3 tabs stale | `willUpdate` in layout | Re-call `detailContext.provide()` when `loaderData` changes | | `setHeaderConfig` silent | Call timing | Call after `super.connectedCallback()` | | `navigate()` no effect | Path format | App-relative path: `/record/incident/abc` not `/aiux/myapp/...` | | `this.server` undefined | Base class | Extend `AIUXWidgetElement`, not `AIUXElement` | | `this` undefined in `client_tools` | Function type | Use `function(args) {}` not arrow function in `definition` | | i18n raw keys | `required_translations` | Register string in widget metadata | | Memory leaks | `disconnectedCallback` | Clean up all observers, listeners, timers |

## ANALYZE Mode
Load: `references/quality/audit-checklist.md`, `references/quality/best-practices-checklist.md`
10-category audit: Structure → Base classes → SSR safety → Styling → i18n → Accessibility → Performance → Security → Observability → Chat integration.

## Key Imports
| Import | From | Purpose | | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | | `html`, `css`, `nothing`, `isServer` | `lit` | Templates, styles, SSR guard | | `customElement`, `property`, `state`, `query` | `lit/decorators.js` | Lit decorators | | `classMap` | `lit/directives/class-map.js` | Conditional CSS classes | | `repeat` | `lit/directives/repeat.js` | Keyed list rendering | | `cache` | `lit/directives/cache.js` | State-switching templates | | `AIUXElement`, `AIUXWidgetElement`, `WithData`, `withWidgetContext` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Base classes | | `decorators`, `createContext`, `getHeaders` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Platform APIs | | `configProperty`, `externalConfig` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Config decorators (widget) | | `elementId` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Config binding — auto-imported by the `aiux-config-id` desugar; import by hand only inside `layout` templates | | `aiuxFetch`, `fetchDataResource` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Client fetch + data broker | | `isPluginActive`, `getSystemProperty`, `getLogger` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | Plugin checks, logging | | `userContext`, `getAMBService` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-core` | User context, real-time | | `i18n`, `locationService`, `recordWatcherService` | `@servicenow/aiux-services` | Platform services | | `navigate`, `getGlobalRouter` | `@servicenow/aiux-client` | Navigation | | `navLayoutContext`, `setHeaderConfig`, `setPageActions` | `@servicenow/aiux-components-nav` | Nav shell | | `lazyImage` | `@servicenow/aiux-directive-lazy-image` | SSR-safe images | | `icon` | `@servicenow/aiux-directive-icon` | Icon directive | | `createLogger` | `@servicenow/aiux-observability` | Server-side logging | | `setDocumentTitle` | `utils/document-title.js` | Browser tab title (WCAG) |
> **Before importing any `@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-<x>` subpath, confirm the package directory exists.** These subpaths are externalised, so a non-existent one passes the build and blanks the page at runtime. See Module Resolution Traps in `lux-ref-foundation`.
---
## Base Classes
| Class | Extends | Use when | | -------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | `AIUXElement` | `LitElement` | Pages, layouts, custom components | | `AIUXWidgetElement` | `AIUXElement` | Widgets with `this.server` | | `WithData(AIUXWidgetElement)` | `AIUXWidgetElement` | Widgets that auto-bind `this.data` from server | | `withWidgetContext(AIUXElement)` | `AIUXElement` | Chat-integrated widgets |
---
## Lit Rules
1. **Extend `AIUXElement` or `AIUXWidgetElement`** — never plain `LitElement` 2. **`static properties = {}`** in JS, `@property()`/`@state()` in TS — declare every mutable property 3. **`classMap`** for conditional classes — `class=${classMap({'btn': true, 'active': isActive})}` 4. **`nothing`** in child/content positions only 5. **Dispatch events** for state owned by parent — `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('...', {bubbles: true, composed: true}))` 6. **Reactive state + `classMap`** for visual mutations 7. **Namespace-scoped event names** — `aiux-widget:sort-change` 8. **Event delegation in loops** — `data-*` attributes + single bound handler on container
---
## SSR Golden Rule
```js import {isServer} from 'lit';
connectedCallback() { super.connectedCallback(); if (!isServer) { window.addEventListener('resize', this._onResize); } } ```
Guard in: `constructor`, `connectedCallback`, `render`, `willUpdate`, `static async loader`, module top-level. No guard needed in: `firstUpdated`, `updated`, `disconnectedCallback`, event handlers.
---
## Server Script (Widget Only)
```js export default function server(data, _options, input) { // data → response object; assign fields to return them to client // _options → widget instance config from page editor // input → params from this.server.get({...}) // Priority: input > options > hardcoded default } ```
The build pipeline (Rollup) compiles `export default function` into an IIFE at deploy time.
Client call:
```js const response = await this.server.get({action: 'getItems', limit: 50}); ```

## Styling
Load: `references/design/css-custom-properties.md` before writing any CSS.
### `:host` by page type
```js /* Standard page */ :host { display: block; } /* List page */ :host { display: contents; } /* required for aiux-list-connected */ /* Widget */ :host { display: block; height: 100%; } /* Dashboard/home */ :host { display: block; min-height: 100%; container-type: inline-size; } ```
### Token quick-reference
| Need | Token | Tailwind class | | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------- | | Default / primary text | `var(--color-text-primary, #000)` | `text-text-primary` | | Subdued text | `var(--color-text-secondary, #4d4c4a)` | `text-text-secondary` | | Card background | `var(--color-base-100, #fff)` | `bg-base-100` | | Page background | `var(--color-base-200, #f2f2f2)` | `bg-base-200` | | Border | `var(--color-base-300, #e5e7eb)` | `border-base-300` |
Always include hex fallback in `static styles`. Card surfaces: `bg-base-100 shadow-sm`.
### Self-constraining visual components
A component that sizes itself from a percentage or viewBox (SVG charts, gauges, media) must carry its own size ceiling in its **own** `static styles` — never rely only on a parent page's class or on Tailwind layout classes. Parent `static styles` and the global Tailwind sheet are not guaranteed to be in effect at first paint, so a `width: 100%` SVG renders at full container width for one frame and then snaps down. The symptom is "huge on first load, correct after navigating".
```js /* In the component itself, not the host page */ :host { display: block; max-width: 9rem; } svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; } ```
### Text overflow protection
All user-facing text elements (titles, subtitles, descriptions) must remain visible and legible at 320px viewport width without horizontal overflow. Use Tailwind utility classes in the template for any text element that receives dynamic or prop-driven content:
```html <span class="break-words max-w-full">${this.title}</span> ```
Reserve `static styles` for values Tailwind cannot express (`:host`, keyframes, pseudo-elements).

# AIUXElement Foundation

## Base Classes

### AIUXElement

Extends `LitElement`. Base class for all AIUX components — pages, layouts, and custom components.

```js
import {AIUXElement} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
import {html, css} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';

@customElement('my-app-element')
export class MyElement extends AIUXElement {
  static styles = css`
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  `;
  render() {
    return html`<div>Hello</div>`;
  }
}
```

### AIUXWidgetElement

Extends `AIUXElement`. Adds `this.server` for GlideRecord/GlideQuery communication and global adopted stylesheets. Used for standalone widgets.

```js
import {AIUXWidgetElement, decorators} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';
const {name, description, discoverable, bestFor} = decorators;

@customElement('aiux-my-widget')
@discoverable(true)
@name('My Widget')
@description('What this widget does')
@bestFor('When to use this widget')
@server('./server.js')
export default class MyWidget extends AIUXWidgetElement { ... }
```

Key differences from `AIUXElement`:

- `this.server.get({action, ...params})` — calls server script
- `this.server.update()` — re-fetch default data
- `this.trackEvent(name, detail)` — analytics
- Global styles adopted automatically (Tailwind + DaisyUI available in shadow DOM)
- `@server` decorator to bind server-side script

### WithData Mixin

Auto-binds server data to `this.data`. Use when the widget simply renders server-provided data.

```js
import {WithData, AIUXWidgetElement} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';

export default class MyWidget extends WithData(AIUXWidgetElement) {
  render() {
    // this.data is automatically populated from server script's `data` object
    const items = this.data?.items || [];
    return html`<ul>
      ${items.map(i => html`<li>${i.name}</li>`)}
    </ul>`;
  }
}
```

### withWidgetContext Mixin

Enables bidirectional widget ↔ AI chat communication. See `references/chat-integration.md` for full API.

```js
import {AIUXElement, withWidgetContext} from '@servicenow/aiux-components-core';

class MyWidget extends withWidgetContext(AIUXElement) {
  static client_tools = { ... };
  static aiContext = { description: '...', bestFor: '...' };
  firstUpdated() { this.setAiContext({key: 'value'}); }
}
```

## Reactive Properties and State

### With decorators (TS or decorator-enabled JS)

```js
import {property, state, query} from 'lit/decorators.js';

@property({type: String}) label = '';       // public, reflects to attribute
@state() _loading = false;                  // internal, no attribute
@query('#input') _inputEl;                  // DOM reference
```

### Without decorators (plain JS)

```js
static properties = {
  label: {type: String},
  _loading: {type: Boolean, state: true},
  _items: {type: Array, state: true}
};
```

**Rules:**

- Every entry MUST include a `type` key
- Internal state MUST have `state: true`
- All properties MUST be initialized with defaults in `constructor()`
- Declare only the component's own properties — Lit merges the prototype chain automatically

---

## Lifecycle Methods

| Method                   | When                | Key rules                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `constructor()`          | Instantiation       | Always call `super()`. Initialize all properties. No DOM access.                        |
| `connectedCallback()`    | Attached to DOM     | Always call `super.connectedCallback()`. Start data fetch, add listeners.               |
| `willUpdate(changed)`    | Before every render | Sync derived state. Re-provide scoped context on navigation. No `this.requestUpdate()`. |
| `render()`               | Each update cycle   | Return `html` template. Pure — no side effects, no mutations.                           |
| `firstUpdated()`         | After first render  | Client-only init (focus, scroll, third-party libs).                                     |
| `updated(changed)`       | After every render  | React to changes. No `this.update()`.                                                   |
| `disconnectedCallback()` | Removed from DOM    | Always call `super.disconnectedCallback()`. Clean up all resources.                     |

### Resource Cleanup (disconnectedCallback)

**All resources acquired in lifecycle MUST be released:**

| Resource                | Setup                                 | Cleanup                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `addEventListener`      | `connectedCallback`                   | `removeEventListener` in `disconnectedCallback` |
| `IntersectionObserver`  | `new IntersectionObserver(...)`       | `.disconnect()`                                 |
| `ResizeObserver`        | `new ResizeObserver(...)`             | `.disconnect()`                                 |
| `MutationObserver`      | `new MutationObserver(...)`           | `.disconnect()`                                 |
| `setTimeout`            | `setTimeout(...)`                     | `clearTimeout(...)`                             |
| `setInterval`           | `setInterval(...)`                    | `clearInterval(...)`                            |
| `requestAnimationFrame` | `rAF(...)`                            | `cancelAnimationFrame(...)`                     |
| `AbortController`       | `new AbortController()`               | `.abort()`                                      |
| Event subscriptions     | `emitter.on(...)`                     | `emitter.off(...)`                              |
| Record watcher          | `recordWatcherService.subscribe(...)` | `.unsubscribe()`                                |
| Scoped context          | `ctx.provide(this, ...)`              | `ctx.unprovide(this)`                           |

```js
connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  this._observer = new IntersectionObserver(this._onIntersect);
  this._observer.observe(this);
  document.addEventListener('scroll', this._onScroll);
  this._timer = setInterval(this._poll, 5000);
}

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  this._observer?.disconnect();
  document.removeEventListener('scroll', this._onScroll);
  clearInterval(this._timer);
}
```

## Event Handler Binding

Bind handlers in the constructor to ensure stable references:

```js
constructor() {
  super();
  this._handleClick = this._handleClick.bind(this);
  this._handleKeyDown = this._handleKeyDown.bind(this);
}
```

For loops, use `data-*` attributes with a single bound handler:

```js
${items.map(item => html`<li data-id=${item.id} @click=${this._handleSelect}>${item.name}</li>`)}
_handleSelect(e) { const id = e.currentTarget.dataset.id; ... }
```
